defect: the BPE tokenizer path dropped the BOS token
mechanism: tokenizer.ggml.add_bos_token is parsed at tokenizer.rs:190 and passed only to LlamaSpmTokenizer. The BPE path delegates to the tokenizers crate, and a GGUF-converted BPE tokenizer carries no post-processor, so nothing prepended BOS.
why_it_looked_like_three_problems: Qwen2.5 declares add_bos_token false and was unaffected, so the one bug presented as 'two adapter families are broken and one works'

evidence_after.qwen: [785, 6722, 315, 9625, 374] — still no BOS, which is correct for Qwen
evidence_after.match: all three now agree with llama.cpp exactly

llama.before: ' a good thing to do the same as the same as the'
llama.after: ' Paris, the largest city in which is located in'

deepseek.before: ' is is is is is is is'
deepseek.verdict: STILL FAIL, different signature, so BOS was necessary but not sufficient here

llama_speed.reading: correctness and speed were two separate defects. llama.rs is 648 lines with 24 Metal references against qwen_dense's 9161 and 465, and the BOS fix does not touch that.

what_this_does_not_fix.deepseek_correctness: a second defect remains, now showing as repeated '!' rather than repeated ' is'

guard: the golden gate was updated deliberately, and it caught this change first: same input sha, output moved ee12bbd4 -> a000b6f0. That is the input-pinning fix working.

deepseek_second_defect.CORRECTION: the previous entry here said the logits carry no signal and argmax is pinned to token 0. That was generalized from a single sample and is wrong.

measured_properly.determinism: four runs, same prompt, same seed, temperature 0: identical output every time

samples.The capital of France is: ' t t t t t t'

deepseek_second_defect.what_that_shows: the forward carries real signal: ' if' after 'def fibonacci(n):' is contextually correct, so the experts, router and head are contributing something. The failure is that it locks into repetition immediately after the first token or two.
deepseek_second_defect.corrected_diagnosis: plausible-first-token followed by immediate repetition is the signature of state that is not advancing between decode steps, which points at the KV cache or position handling rather than at an empty forward
deepseek_second_defect.why_the_earlier_reading_was_wrong: '!' is token 0 and I treated one prompt's output as the general case. Three prompts and four repeats would have shown otherwise, and cost about a minute.
deepseek_second_defect.next_probe: log seq_slot, seq_len and the argmax id per decode step for eight steps. If seq_len advances while the token repeats, the read length or the expert routing is wrong rather than the write.
deepseek_second_defect.status: OPEN, narrowed to 'stops advancing at step 4' with five causes eliminated

bisect_by_token_count.token_3: ' if' — correct, this is exactly right Python
bisect_by_token_count.reading: the forward is correct for three tokens and then reproduces token 3 indefinitely. This is not an empty forward and not a wrong forward; it is a forward that stops advancing.

eliminated: empty logits: output varies with the prompt and the first three tokens are right
non-determinism: four runs at temperature 0 are identical
BOS out of range: bos id 100000 against vocab_size 102400
frozen KV slot: seq_slot is self.kv.seq_len and deepseek_v2.rs:3016 advances it in the Wedge C path
tokenizer: tokenization matches llama.cpp exactly after the BOS fix
deepseek_second_defect.still_open: what makes token 4 repeat token 3 when position, slot and sequence length are all correct. The remaining candidates are the KV length passed to mla_decode and MoE expert selection.

trace_result.instrumentation: HAWKING_DS_TRACE=1 prints pos, seq_slot and seq_len per step
trace_result.measured: prompt is 7 tokens; the trace runs pos=0..6 then decode continues pos=7,8,9
trace_result.verdict: position and KV slot bookkeeping are CORRECT throughout. seq_slot equals pos and seq_len advances by one every step.
trace_result.my_false_start: an earlier trace read pos=0..9 and I took it for decode starting at 0, i.e. decode overwriting the prompt's KV. It was prefill plus decode with the output truncated by head -10. Checking the prompt length against the trace took one command and refuted it.
eliminated_additionally: decode does not overwrite prefill KV
positions are not stuck or reset

prefill_finding.observed: prefill emits one trace line per prompt token, so it runs token-by-token through the same Wedge C decode path
prefill_finding.consistent_with: 91.7 ms per prompt token, which is roughly this model's decode cost, against llama.cpp's 0.76 ms
prefill_finding.implication: DeepSeek has no batched prefill at all, which is a separate and larger gap than the 14B's batch-8 ceiling
